nary_nodes.label: Bulgaria wins Eurovision
evidence: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest on Sunday with Dara's catchy floor-filler "Bangaranga" sweeping the 70th edition of the world's biggest live televised music event and pushing into second place Israel, whose participation had triggered a major boycott.

Bulgaria has missed the last three editions of the glitzy extravaganza but took the crown in Vienna for the first time ever, overtaking Israel at the very end as the points came in, with Romania finishing third.

nary_nodes.label: Israel finishes second
evidence: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest on Sunday with Dara's catchy floor-filler "Bangaranga" sweeping the 70th edition of the world's biggest live televised music event and pushing into second place Israel, whose participation had triggered a major boycott.
Bulgaria finished with 516 points, ahead of Israel on 343, Romania on 296, Australia on 287, Italy with 281 and Finland on 279.

nary_nodes.label: Romania finishes third
evidence: Bulgaria has missed the last three editions of the glitzy extravaganza but took the crown in Vienna for the first time ever, overtaking Israel at the very end as the points came in, with Romania finishing third.
Bulgaria finished with 516 points, ahead of Israel on 343, Romania on 296, Australia on 287, Italy with 281 and Finland on 279.

nary_nodes.label: Australia finishes fourth
evidence: Australia's Delta Goodrem, who has sold nine million albums, came fourth after wowing the crowds with her song "Eclipse", which was filled with strong moments, ending with her soaring high on a riser coming up out of a glittering piano.

nary_nodes.label: Countries boycott Eurovision
evidence: Spain, the Netherlands, Ireland, Iceland and Slovenia staged the biggest political boycott in Eurovision history over Israel's participation, citing the war in Gaza.

nary_nodes.label: Protesters march against Israel
evidence: Hundreds of protesters against Israel's inclusion marched near the contest arena before Saturday's final, some holding placards saying "Block Eurovision".
Pro-Palestinian groups also staged an outdoor concert on Friday under the banner "No stage for genocide".

nary_nodes.label: Dara performs Bangaranga
evidence: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest on Sunday with Dara's catchy floor-filler "Bangaranga" sweeping the 70th edition of the world's biggest live televised music event and pushing into second place Israel, whose participation had triggered a major boycott.

nary_nodes.label: Bettan performs Michelle
evidence: Bettan was loudly cheered, though there was a smattering of boos as he performed “Michelle", a rock ballad in Hebrew, French and English.

nary_nodes.label: JJ opens with aria
evidence: JJ had opened Saturday's musical extravaganza with a nod to Austria's grand musical history, singing the "Queen of the Night" aria from composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's 1791 opera "The Magic Flute".

nary_nodes.label: Lampenius performs Liekinheitin
evidence: As the song built to a climax, 56-year-old Lampenius was shredding her bow as she worked her way to the very top of the fingerboard.

nary_nodes.label: Capitanescu performs Choke Me
evidence: Romanian singer Alexandra Capitanescu's switched up the vibe with the 22-year-old's heavy metal song "Choke Me" triggering controversy in the build-up over its repeated lyric: "I want you to choke me".

nary_nodes.label: Goodrem performs Eclipse
evidence: Australia's Delta Goodrem, who has sold nine million albums, came fourth after wowing the crowds with her song "Eclipse", which was filled with strong moments, ending with her soaring high on a riser coming up out of a glittering piano.

nary_nodes.label: Lavina performs
evidence: Serbian metallers Lavina had the deepest throat-shredding growl of the night, the Czech Republic's Daniel Zizka navigated a hall of mirrors, while Lithuania's silver-painted Lion Ceccah brought an air of brooding mystery.

nary_nodes.label: Zizka performs
evidence: Serbian metallers Lavina had the deepest throat-shredding growl of the night, the Czech Republic's Daniel Zizka navigated a hall of mirrors, while Lithuania's silver-painted Lion Ceccah brought an air of brooding mystery.

nary_nodes.label: Ceccah performs
evidence: Serbian metallers Lavina had the deepest throat-shredding growl of the night, the Czech Republic's Daniel Zizka navigated a hall of mirrors, while Lithuania's silver-painted Lion Ceccah brought an air of brooding mystery.

nary_nodes.label: Fans ejected from semifinal
evidence: Earlier in the week, four people were ejected for trying to disrupt his semifinal performance.

nary_nodes.label: JJ hands trophy to Dara
evidence: Johannes Pietsch, known as JJ, who won Eurovision 2025 for Austria with his song "Wasted Love", handed over the winner's trophy to Dara.

nary_nodes.label: Dara says everything possible
evidence: "Everything is possible: Bulgaria just won Eurovision!" Dara told a press conference.

nary_nodes.label: Dara says she breaks rules
evidence: "I really like breaking rules. I'm really good with following my rules – not anybody else's.

nary_nodes.label: Dara says they wanted new
evidence: "We wanted to give to the audience something new and fresh, something that is not expected."

nary_nodes.label: Pekanov hails magnificent story
evidence: Bulgarian Deputy Prime Minister Atanas Pekanov on Facebook hailed a "magnificent story of immense talent, tireless effort, and faith in success, against all criticism".

nary_nodes.label: Bongola says invitation affront
evidence: "Inviting Israel on such a beautiful stage as the Eurovision Song Contest stage is an affront to all the people who believe in humanity, who believe in love and togetherness," said Congolese-Austrian artist Patrick Bongola, one of the organisers.

nary_nodes.label: Dara says Bangaranga feeling
evidence: "Bangaranga, it's a feeling that everybody has got in themselves," Dara said earlier Sunday as the votes were coming in.
"It's the moment that you choose to lead through love and not fear, and this is a special energy that I know everybody has got in themselves."

nary_nodes.label: Katerina says stunned
evidence: "I didn't like the song at first... but I saw it, I saw the performance, and I was stunned," said Katerina, a Eurovision fan from Greece.
